learningObjective: Understand cp.async: async GMEM→SMEM copy bypassing registers, introduced on Ampere.

canonicalClaims.claim: `cp.async` (Ampere sm_80+) copies data from global memory to shared memory asynchronously, bypassing the register file; completion is synchronized with `cp.async.commit_group` and `cp.async.wait_group`, enabling software-pipelined kernels (e.g., multi-stage GEMM).
conditions: Ampere or newer hardware; CUDA 11+ toolchain.
nonImplications: Does not imply auto-completion; explicit wait is required.
Does not imply small copies always benefit.

misconceptions.claim: `cp.async` is a synchronous load through registers.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is genuinely async and bypasses registers.
cp.async is Ampere (sm_80)+; Hopper adds TMA on top.

misconceptions.claim: cp.async completes automatically after a fixed number of cycles.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Explicit `wait_group` / barrier is needed to observe completion.

implementationFacts: Multi-stage GEMM pipelines (CUTLASS `Sm80MultiStage*`) rely on cp.async.
Hopper TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) extends this with shape-aware bulk transfers.
